reactions.architecture: asymmetric two-tail Ugi-derived alpha-amino-amide ionizable lipid

sources.locator: AGILE; Figures 1b and 2a; Methods, Experimental library
sources.notes: The 1,200-member AGILE measured library supplies A/B/C components and full products. This qualified transform is validated by exact reconstruction of all 1,200 products, not by the released fixed-core wildcard-stitching notebook.
Ground-truth substrate/product tuples used for the qualification correctness gate.

reactions.selectivity_policy: Acid-free Ugi three-component condensation forming an alpha-amino amide: an N-H amine and an aldehyde condense to an imine, an isocyanide adds, and hydration yields R1-NH-CH(R2)-C(=O)-NH-R4. Reactive handles: an amine with at least one N-H (primary or secondary; tertiary amines are inert), an aldehyde carbon bearing exactly one H (ketones are inert), and a terminal (degree-1) isocyanide carbon (internal nitrile carbons are inert). Substrates with multiple N-H amines enumerate one alpha-amino-amide regiochemical product per reactive amine; all are route-certified and deduplicated downstream.
reactions.stereochemistry_policy: Preserve any substrate stereochemistry. The new alpha carbon stereocenter is left unspecified, matching the released AGILE product SMILES.
reactions.protonation_and_salt_policy: Register neutral full-molecule products under the frozen compose_lipid canonicalization contract; no neutralization or salt stripping is applied and none is required for these substrates.

known_positive_examples.reason: Single-amine substrate reconstructs the released product exactly (1 enumerated product).
Tail-length homolog reconstructs exactly under the same transform.

known_negative_examples.reason: Tertiary-amine-only substrate has no N-H handle; the transform yields no product.
A ketone is not an aldehyde (no C-H on the carbonyl); the transform yields no product.
A nitrile carbon is internal (degree 2), not a terminal isocyanide carbon; the transform yields no product.
